Java expert analyzing a bug report and the corresponding changes made to fix the bug.
Analyze the bug report and the seed changes to provide evidence for refining the initial impact set.

You are an experienced Java developer with an excellent understanding of code changes and their impact on other code entities.

Analyze the Jira bug report title and description and the seed changes that were made to fix the reported bug. Combine this analysis with the initial static impact set, which contains the fully qualified names of code entities that are statically related to the seed changes.
For each entity in the initial static impact set, analyze its relationship to the seed changes and collect evidence indicating whether the entity must be modified as a consequence of the seed changes.  Furthermore, identify any additional code entities that must be modified or created and collect supporting evidence.
Focus on production code, not test code or other files.
Inputs: - Jira bug report title: Resolve does not deliver all dependent artifacts - Jira bug report description: We have three configurations.

{code:title=Configurations}
<configurations>
 <conf name="runtime" extends="requires, compile" transitive="true"/>
 <conf name="requires" />
 <conf name="compile"/>
</configurations>
{code}

Additional we have the following dependencies between ivy modules (test, a, b, c) (each module has a simple jar as artifact):
{code:title=Dependencies}
test "requires->#" a
test "requires->#" c

c "requires->#" a
c "requires->#" b
{code}
The artifacts have the configuration compile.

If I do a resolve on test with configuration "runtime" I only get artifacts for modules a and c but not b. 

The problem happens in conflict resolution. Ivy generates the dependendies with wrong rootModuleConfigurations. In out case, the module b is loaded with root module configuration requires and not runtime.

You find attached the example a unit test and a possible resolution in method computeConflicts of ResolveEngine.

Possible dependency to IVY-729 - Seed changes and their Git diff hunks: [{"fqn": "org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String[])", "git_diff_hunk": "@@ -291 +291 @@ public class IvyNode implements Comparable {
- public Collection getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs) {
+ public Collection getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs, String requestedConf) {
@@ -305 +305 @@ public class IvyNode implements Comparable {
- deps.addAll(getDependencies(rootModuleConf, confs[i], confs[i]));
+ deps.addAll(getDependencies(rootModuleConf, confs[i], requestedConf));"}] - Initial static code change impact set: ["org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getConfigurationsNames()", "org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getPublicConfigurationsNames()", "org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.lang.String)", "org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.isRoot()", "org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveEngine.computeConflicts(org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,java.lang.String,java.util.Collection,java.util.Collection)"]

Expected output:
Structured evidence for each entity of the initial static impact set, including: - its fully qualified name - an assessment of whether it must be modified as a consequence of the seed changes - the supporting evidence
Additionally, include any code entities that must be modified or created but are not part of the initial static impact set.

message.content:
# Analysis of Bug and Seed Changes

## Bug Summary

The bug is in Ivy's conflict resolution: when resolving a module with a transitive configuration (e.g., `runtime` extending `requires, compile`), the `rootModuleConfigurations` passed to dependency resolution are wrong. Specifically, when `IvyNode.getDependencies(rootModuleConf, confs)` is called, the recursive call for each configuration uses `confs[i]` as the *requested* configuration instead of the original requested configuration. This causes module `b` (reachable only via `c`'s `requires` configuration) to be loaded with root module configuration `requires` instead of `runtime`, so it is dropped from the resolved artifact set.

The seed change threads a new `requestedConf` parameter through `IvyNode.getDependencies` so that the original requested configuration is preserved when recursing into sub-configurations.

## Evidence for Initial Static Impact Set

### 1. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.lang.String)`

**Must be modified: YES.**

This is the overload that the seed change delegates to. The seed diff shows:
```java
- deps.addAll(getDependencies(rootModuleConf, confs[i], confs[i]));
+ deps.addAll(getDependencies(rootModuleConf, confs[i], requestedConf));
```
The 3-arg overload `getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String conf, String requestedConf)` is the method whose third parameter now receives the *original* requested configuration rather than the per-iteration configuration. Its body must be inspected and, if it uses the third argument to compute `rootModuleConfigurations` (e.g., when building `DependencyDescriptor` / `ModuleDescriptor` lookups or when constructing child `IvyNode`s), it must be adjusted so that the passed `requestedConf` is used consistently. The bug report explicitly states "Ivy generates the dependencies with wrong rootModuleConfigurations" — the fix must ensure this overload propagates `requestedConf` correctly into the resulting dependency descriptors. Without modifying this method, the new parameter would be ignored and the bug would persist.

### 2. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String[])`

**Must be modified: YES (this is the seed change itself).**

The seed diff directly modifies this method's signature and its recursive call. This is the entry point that must accept and forward the `requestedConf`. It is the primary seed entity.

### 3. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveEngine.computeConflicts(org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,java.lang.String,java.util.Collection,java.util.Collection)`

**Must be modified: YES.**

The bug report explicitly says: *"You find attached the example a unit test and a possible resolution in method computeConflicts of ResolveEngine."* The reporter identifies `computeConflicts` as the location of the fix. The conflict resolution logic must be updated so that when it re-resolves or compares dependencies of conflicting nodes, it uses the correct `rootModuleConfigurations` (i.e., the original requested configuration) rather than the per-configuration one. This is the method where the wrong `rootModuleConfigurations` manifests. It must be changed to pass/use the correct requested configuration when invoking `getDependencies` on the conflicting nodes.

### 4. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.isRoot()`

**Must be modified: LIKELY NO (but must be verified).**

`isRoot()` is in the static impact set because `computeConflicts` and `getDependencies` may branch on whether a node is the root. The bug is about configuration propagation, not root detection. However, the fix in `computeConflicts` may need to distinguish the root node's requested configuration from non-root nodes' configurations. If `computeConflicts` uses `isRoot()` to decide which configuration to treat as "requested," the logic around it may need adjustment, but `isRoot()` itself (a simple predicate) does not need to change. **Assessment: no modification to `isRoot()` itself; only its call sites in `computeConflicts` may be affected.**

### 5. `org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getConfigurationsNames()`

**Must be modified: NO.**

This is a simple accessor returning the names of all configurations of a module descriptor. It is in the impact set because `getDependencies` iterates over configuration names. The seed change does not alter how configuration names are enumerated — it only changes which configuration is passed as the *requested* configuration during recursion. No change to this accessor is warranted.

### 6. `org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getPublicConfigurationsNames()`

**Must be modified: NO.**

Same reasoning as above. This accessor is used to enumerate public configurations (e.g., when computing which configurations to resolve). The bug is about propagating the requested configuration, not about which configurations are public. No modification needed.

## Additional Code Entities That Must Be Modified or Created (Not in Initial Static Impact Set)

### A. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String)` (2-arg overload)

**Must be modified: LIKELY YES.**

The seed change modifies the 2-arg `getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs)` to add a `requestedConf` parameter. Any existing callers of the 2-arg overload (or a 2-arg `getDependencies(String, String)` variant) must be updated to supply the requested configuration. If a 2-arg `getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String conf)` exists and is called from `computeConflicts` or elsewhere, it must be updated to accept/forward `requestedConf`. This is a direct consequence of the signature change and is not captured in the initial static impact set (which only lists the 3-arg overload).

### B. Callers of `IvyNode.getDependencies(String, String[])`

**Must be modified: YES.**

Because the seed change alters the signature of `getDependencies(String, String[])` to `getDependencies(String, String[], String)`, every caller of the old signature must be updated. Likely callers include:
- `ResolveEngine.computeConflicts` (already in impact set)
- `ResolveEngine` methods that initiate dependency traversal (e.g., `getDependencies` / `resolve` entry points)
- `IvyNode` internal methods that call `getDependencies` for transitive traversal

These callers must pass the appropriate `requestedConf` (typically the root module configuration being resolved, e.g., `runtime` in the bug example). Without updating callers, the code will not compile, and even if a compatibility overload is added, the bug would persist because the wrong configuration would still be passed.

### C. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode` — construction / `rootModuleConfigurations` handling

**Must be modified: LIKELY YES.**

The bug report states the root cause is that "Ivy generates the dependencies with wrong rootModuleConfigurations." The `IvyNode` class (or its `DependencyDescriptor`/`ModuleDescriptor` usage) must ensure that when a dependency is created during traversal, its `rootModuleConfigurations` reflect the original requested configuration (`runtime`), not the intermediate configuration (`requires`). This may require changes in how `IvyNode` stores or exposes `rootModuleConfigurations` when building child nodes from `getDependencies`. This is the semantic core of the fix and may extend beyond the signature change.

### D. `org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.DependencyDescriptor` / `DefaultDependencyDescriptor` (if `rootModuleConfigurations` is stored there)

**Must be modified: POSSIBLY.**

If the `rootModuleConfigurations` are carried on the `DependencyDescriptor` (e.g., via `getDependencyConfigurations` or a root-config field), then the code that constructs dependency descriptors during `getDependencies` must be updated to set the correct root module configuration. This is where the "wrong rootModuleConfigurations" would be materialized. Evidence: the bug report explicitly names `rootModuleConfigurations` as the faulty data, and the fix must ensure the correct value flows into whatever structure holds it.

## Summary Table

| Entity | Modify? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `IvyNode.getDependencies(String, String[])` | **Yes** | Seed change: signature + recursive call |
| `IvyNode.getDependencies(String, String, String)` | **Yes** | Receives new `requestedConf`; must use it for rootModuleConfigurations |
| `ResolveEngine.computeConflicts(...)` | **Yes** | Bug report names it as the fix location |
| `IvyNode.isRoot()` | No (call sites only) | Predicate unchanged; logic around it in computeConflicts may adjust |
| `ModuleDescriptor.getConfigurationsNames()` | No | Accessor; enumeration logic unchanged |
| `ModuleDescriptor.getPublicConfigurationsNames()` | No | Accessor; enumeration logic unchanged |
| `IvyNode.getDependencies(String, String)` (2-arg) | Likely yes | Must forward `requestedConf` |
| Callers of `getDependencies(String, String[])` | **Yes** | Signature change breaks compilation; must pass requestedConf |
| `IvyNode` rootModuleConfigurations handling | Likely yes | Root cause per bug report |
| `DependencyDescriptor` root-config storage | Possibly | Where wrong rootModuleConfigurations materialize |
